components.intent: Organize the workshop as an asymmetrical cluster of distinct fabrication, public, service, and elevated studio pavilions.
Establish the double-height fabrication hall as a freestanding central pavilion rather than one side of a supporting bar.
Extend the public exhibition route into a separate linear pavilion on the eastern edge of the cluster.
Place service and loading in a compact detached pavilion on the opposite side of the fabrication hall.
Concentrate the upper studios in an elevated pavilion offset from the fabrication hall and aligned with the public wing.

constraint_responses.rationale: The supplied program bounds footprint and total floor area but provides no defensible allocation of net area among the four functions, so net area remains unresolved in this schematic alternative.

proposal.label: Pinwheel workshop cluster with elevated studio pavilion
proposal.rationale: The 20-cell footprint represents 2000 square metres on the declared 100-square-metre grid and falls within the current 1500–2200-square-metre footprint range. Separating the public, service, and studio masses around the double-height hall creates a materially different clustered topology while retaining every declared function. The proposal remains coarse massing and does not assert detailed circulation, structural support, constructability, net-area compliance, or validation.
proposal.typology_hypothesis: An asymmetrical pinwheel of specialized pavilions replaces the compact hall-and-bar arrangement: fabrication forms the tall center, exhibition and service occupy opposing ground-level arms, and studios become an offset elevated pavilion.

components.intent: Organize the workshop as a fabrication hall paired with a compact public, service, and studio bar.
Provide the declared double-height fabrication workspace as the dominant volume.
Form a public-facing exhibition zone beside the fabrication hall and primary approach.
Concentrate service and loading at one end of the supporting bar.
Stack upper studios over the public and service bar with adjacency to the tall hall.

constraint_responses.rationale: The supplied records declare footprint and total-floor-area ranges but no bounded net-area allocation; this schematic option therefore preserves net area as unresolved.

existing_option_projection.label: Double-height fabrication hall with stacked studio and public-service bar
existing_option_projection.rationale: The 15-cell footprint represents 1500 square metres at the declared grid basis, meeting the lower bound of the current footprint range. The primary approach aligns with the center of the compact mass, the fabrication hall receives the dominant double-height volume, and studios are stacked above the exhibition and service bar without asserting detailed circulation or constructability.
existing_option_projection.typology_hypothesis: A compact industrial hall-and-bar typology: the double-height fabrication hall occupies the primary mass, while exhibition and loading share a ground-level support bar with studios stacked above.

payload.instructions: Author one schematic option from only the supplied current records. Create the existing DesignComponent tree and its coarse massing volumes in the same proposal. Every volume must have exactly one component owner. Preserve project evidence references and return only the required output object; do not select, persist, execute, or claim validation.

assumptions.statement: The numeric ranges are direct user-declared experiment inputs, preserved as bounded values rather than point defaults.

obligations.statement: Derive bounded net-area hypotheses or preserve net area as unknown.

every zone names only declared level_ids and volume_ids
each connection joins zones containing its relationship source and target nodes and matches relationship directed exactly
